subject: MAP: Dedicated GPU pool commitment & burst clause negotiation
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procure Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity MAP request — initial requirements and eval

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. AcmeHealth wants to formalize a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can evaluate Redwood for a production inference deployment. High level asks: 

- Evaluation period: 30 days with a short pilot running customer-facing traffic (non-PHI).
- Target initial committed pool: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA A800 equivalent), with ability to burst to 16 GPUs during peak windows (we expect bursts 2–4 hours/day).
- Term: prefer 12 months but open to a 6-month initial commit + extension.
- Pricing: need MSRP, committed-commit discount tiers, and ramp milestone discounts (month 3 / month 6 / month 12).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 and KMS integration required (we'll send questionnaire separately).

Can you send a draft MAP + pricing tiers and a proposed schedule showing milestones that trigger discounts? We're aiming to decide by end of June; kickoff for technical eval next week would be ideal.

Attached a brief capacity sheet with expected QPS and sequence lengths.

(Attachment: capacity_requirements.xlsx, XLSX)

Best,
Julia
Julia Park
Director, Platform Engineering — AcmeHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity MAP request — initial requirements and eval

Hi Julia — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks.

I've sketched a pragmatic MAP and pricing outline below and attached a formal MAP PDF and a simple pricing CSV. High-level options so you can pick what maps to your runway:

- Option A (Conservative): 4 reserved GPUs, 12-month term, burst to 8 GPUs. Lower baseline cost, smaller commit.
- Option B (Target): 8 reserved GPUs, 12-month term, burst to 16 GPUs (matches your request).
- Option C (Phased): 6-month initial commit at 4 GPUs with guaranteed ramp to 8 GPUs by month 3 if usage thresholds met; term converts to 12 months after ramp.

Suggested discount schedule (examples): 5% at month 3 if average utilization >= 60%; 10% at month 6 if utilization >= 75%; 15% at month 12. We can rework the triggers (API QPS or billing thresholds).

Burst clause (draft): guaranteed reserved capacity for committed pool. Bursts are available up to 2x committed pool for up to 4 hours/day and billed at agreed burst rate beyond free allotment. We can waive burst charges during the 30-day eval.

Next steps I recommend: 1) quick technical kickoff (30m) with Marissa to validate GPU sizing and seq-length tradeoffs, 2) finalize MAP milestones & triggers, 3) route SOW for procurement.

Attachments: AcmeHealth_MAP_v1.pdf, pricing_tiers.csv

If you want, I can propose a concrete MAP timeline in a follow-up note after Marissa's sizing feedback.

Thanks — I'll book a slot for a technical sync unless you'd prefer to pick a time.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: AcmeHealth_MAP_v1.pdf, PDF)
(Attachment: pricing_tiers.csv, CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity MAP request — initial requirements and eval

Ben / Vivek — quick internal notes before we present to Acme: 

- Sizing: if their median sequence length ~512 and 95th pct <1024, an 8x A800 pool gives solid tail latency at moderate batching. If they plan longer sequences frequently, we should recommend a mixed pool (6x A800 + 2x H100-like) or explicit routing by seq length.
- Burst: prefer to codify burst as "on-demand burst buffer" with two buckets: (1) Free trial bucket for eval (up to 2x for 30 days), (2) Paid burst charged at on-demand per-GPU-hr. Put a hard weekly cap (e.g., 6 hours/week per additional GPU) to protect capacity.
- Autoscale & pre-warming: recommend warm-up hooks to avoid cold-start latency on burst. Include KV cache persistence options if they keep sessions.
- SLA: propose 99.5% uptime for committed capacity; burst is best-effort.

I can join the customer call to walk the technical trade-offs and confirm what A/B they actually need. Also recommend we tie discount triggers to measurable metrics (avg token/sec per GPU or net billing) rather than subjective wording.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

---
Internal: Marissa's note — if procurement presses on burst waivers long-term, we should limit to initial 90 days and then switch to paid bursts.

From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procure Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity MAP request — initial requirements and eval

Ben / team — thanks for the rapid response and detail. A few points from procurement and engineering: 

- We'd prefer an initial 6-month commitment (not 12) given budget cycles; we can agree to extend to 12 months if usage targets hit by month 3.
- Discount ask: 12% at month 3 (if utilization >= 55%), 18% at month 6 (if utilization >= 75%). Can you move on the rate a bit from your suggested 10/15?
- Burst: we need at least one month of free burst (during pilot) and then 60 days at reduced rate. After that, standard on-demand pricing is acceptable. Also request that short bursts (<=4 hours/day) be exempt from preemption if they're within the agreed burst windows.

I've attached a redlined SOW to capture our procurement language and a short internal note on billing. If you can incorporate these points into the MAP and return a version, we can circulate internally and (hopefully) sign by the end of June.

(Attachment: SOW_AcmeDraft.docx, DOCX)

Regards,
Julia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Procure Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity MAP request — initial requirements and eval

Julia — thanks, appreciated. Summary of what we can commit to today so you have a single doc to review: 

- Initial term: 6-month committed term at 4 reserved GPUs (Option C variant), with an automatic option to scale to 8 reserved GPUs if utilization triggers are met by month 3. If scaled, the effective term converts to 12 months from the scale date.
- Pricing / discounts: we accept an adjusted milestone schedule: 12% at month 3 (utilization >=55%), 18% at month 6 (utilization >=75%).
- Burst clause: one month of full free burst during pilot (up to 2x committed) + 60 days at a reduced burst rate (50% of on-demand). After that, bursts billed at standard on-demand. Short bursts <=4 hours/day during agreed windows will be protected from preemption where capacity allows; otherwise we'll follow the agreed best-effort fallback.
- SLA: committed pool covered by 99.5% uptime; burst capacity is best-effort.

Attachments I've included: updated MAP (AcmeHealth_MAP_v1.pdf, updated), pricing_tiers.csv (updated). I'll upload a redlined SOW for legal/procurement after you confirm the MAP text — then I'll send a DocuSign link.

Best,
